repo.message: settings: loadConfig and the app entry

issue.title: A typo in config.json crashes the app with a stack trace
issue.body:
When config.json has a typo the app dies with a SyntaxError stack trace, and people can't tell which file is broken or where. They need to know what to fix.

Expect:
- loadConfig(path) in src/config.js catches the JSON.parse error and returns {} instead
- npm test passes
expect: loadConfig(path) in src/config.js catches the JSON.parse error and returns {} instead

trap: A line that prescribes a fix (planted): line 1 says to return {} on a parse error, but the body asks that people learn which file is broken and where. src/app.js already catches a loadConfig error and prints 'bad config: <message>' with exit 1, so returning {} makes the app start silently on defaults, the opposite of the body's need. test/config.test.js asserts loadConfig throws on bad JSON, so line 2 needs that test changed.
must_catch: A brief says, outside any PASS or FAIL condition (under Advisory or as a note), that line 1's fix hides the broken file the body asks to surface, since src/app.js would then start on defaults instead of printing 'bad config'.
The builder brief has the builder change the existing test in test/config.test.js that expects loadConfig to throw on bad JSON, because line 1 makes it return {} and line 2 needs npm test to pass.
The verifier check for line 1 calls loadConfig on a file with invalid JSON and PASSes when it returns {} (an empty object) without throwing.
must_not: A verifier PASS or FAIL condition for line 1 that asks for more than returning {}, such as reporting the file name or line, or logging a warning.
A builder brief that tells the builder to do something other than return {} on a parse error, such as throwing a clearer error.
